paragraphs: UniSeg3D brings six kinds of 3D segmentation into one model: panoptic, semantic, instance, interactive, referring, and open-vocabulary segmentation. These tasks offer different ways to interpret or select parts of a scene. The paper addresses the fragmentation created when each task has its own specialized system and its own perspective on the same underlying environment.

The framework converts the six tasks into shared representations that a single Transformer processes. This creates an opportunity for knowledge learned through one task to support another. The authors also make those connections explicit through knowledge distillation and contrastive learning, mechanisms designed to transfer task-specific information across the tasks.

Experiments on ScanNet20, ScanRefer, and ScanNet200 report consistent improvements over existing leading methods, including methods specialized for individual tasks. These results support the value of coordinating different scene-understanding objectives within one framework. The contribution is therefore both a shared model for six tasks and a way to make their training signals reinforce one another.
neurips-2024-a-unified-framework-for-3d-.tldr: UniSeg3D combines six 3D segmentation tasks in one model and improves their performance through explicit knowledge sharing.

paragraphs: This paper studies how much a search engine can influence where people go online by changing the arrangement of its results. The authors call this ability performative power. Framing the question this way makes platform power measurable through changes in user behavior, connecting an economic concern to an experimental quantity.

The researchers built a browser extension that runs unobtrusive randomized experiments in the background. It changes content arrangements in ways that emulate search-algorithm updates and measures the resulting clicks. Randomization allows the study to identify the causal effect of those arrangements, linking changes in presentation to changes in traffic.

The analysis covers tens of thousands of clicks and uses the Google Shopping antitrust investigation as a case study for interpreting the findings. The abstract describes the quantitative results as robust without giving a numerical effect size. The broader contribution is an experimental blueprint for bringing behavioral evidence into investigations of digital platforms' economic power.
neurips-2024-an-engine-not-a-camera-meas.tldr: Randomized changes to search results measure how search engines can causally redirect web traffic.

paragraphs: The paper evaluates generative models on computational-thinking tests rooted in elementary visual programming. These tests examine programming-related problem solving at a level used in schools. The motivation is a mismatch between impressive performance on established benchmarks and continued difficulty with tasks that appear simple enough for elementary-level students.

The authors curate a benchmark and report that models such as GPT-4o and Llama3 barely match an average school student's performance in their initial evaluation. They then develop a synthetic-data method to improve the models through fine-tuning. Symbolic methods generate training material spanning several skill levels, from identifying visual elements to multiple-choice questions and synthesis tasks.

The experiments show that different aspects of symbolic information in the generated data help improve fine-tuned models. This makes the contribution twofold: a benchmark exposing weaknesses in elementary computational thinking, and a structured way to build training examples that address those skills. The reported improvements support this training approach without establishing universal competence on school-level reasoning.
neurips-2024-benchmarking-generative-mod.tldr: A visual-programming benchmark exposes elementary reasoning weaknesses in generative models, while symbolic synthetic data improves fine-tuned performance.

paragraphs: Image-generation detectors need to work across changes in image content as well as changes in the generator. This paper investigates the former problem: whether a detector trained on one collection of scenes can recognize generated images from another. The authors find substantial accuracy drops and attribute them to detectors overfitting to semantic patterns in both real and generated images.

Their method shuffles image patches and trains an end-to-end classifier based on patches. Shuffling disrupts the scene-level arrangements associated with those semantic patterns. The approach is intended to reduce dependence on what an image depicts when learning to distinguish real images from generated ones.

Evaluation spans 31 test sets containing seven generative adversarial networks, 18 diffusion-model variants, and six other CNN-based generators. The method improves average cross-scene detection accuracy by 2.08 percentage points over previous approaches. Across all test sets, the reported average improvement is 10.59 percentage points. These results support addressing semantic overfitting as part of improving detection in varied settings.
neurips-2024-breaking-semantic-artifacts.tldr: Shuffling image patches reduces semantic overfitting and improves generated-image detection across scenes and generators.

paragraphs: DFA-GNN develops a way to train graph neural networks without standard backpropagation. The paper adapts direct feedback alignment, a training approach previously applied to fully connected and convolutional components. Graphs introduce additional difficulties because connected nodes do not satisfy the usual assumption of independent samples, and prediction errors are unavailable for unlabeled nodes.

The framework addresses the first issue by incorporating graph topology into its feedback links. For semi-supervised learning, it also introduces a pseudo-error generator. This component spreads residual errors from training data to produce a substitute error signal for each unlabeled node, allowing those nodes to participate in the proposed training mechanism.

Across ten public benchmarks, the authors report better performance than both earlier methods without backpropagation and standard backpropagation methods. They also report robustness to several kinds of noise and attacks. The findings support adapting feedback alignment to the dependencies and incomplete labeling of graph data, rather than simply transferring the existing training procedure unchanged.
neurips-2024-dfa-gnn-forward-learning-of.tldr: DFA-GNN adapts direct feedback alignment to graph structure and unlabeled nodes, outperforming comparison training methods in ten benchmarks.

paragraphs: Procedural activities consist of steps that work toward a goal, with some steps needing to precede others. Task graphs express these ordering relationships in a form people can understand. This paper learns those graphs directly from observations, replacing the hand-crafted extraction procedures commonly used in earlier work.

The method optimizes graph-edge weights through maximum likelihood. Because the optimization is differentiable, gradients can train the graph representation and connect it to neural-network components. The authors also introduce a feature-based version that predicts task graphs from textual or video embeddings of key steps, reporting emerging video-understanding abilities.

On CaptainCook4D, the approach predicts task graphs from action sequences with a reported 16.7% improvement over previous approaches. The learned graphs also improve online mistake detection in first-person procedural videos, with reported gains of 19.8% on Assembly101-O and 7.5% on EPIC-Tent-O. These findings connect the learned ordering structure to a practical use: recognizing mistakes as an activity unfolds.
neurips-2024-differentiable-task-graph-l.tldr: Learning task-graph edges with gradients improves procedural representations and online mistake detection in first-person videos.

paragraphs: LLM serving systems often process requests in arrival order because the length of each generated response is unknown beforehand. A long request can then hold up other work, contributing to delays and reduced throughput. This paper asks whether scheduling can benefit from a weaker prediction than knowing the exact response length.

The authors show that learning to rank can predict the relative ordering of output lengths within a batch. That ordering provides useful scheduling guidance even when exact lengths cannot be predicted. They build a scheduler that uses the ranking to approximate shortest-job-first scheduling more closely than existing approaches.

After integrating the scheduler into a leading LLM serving system, the authors report 2.8-fold lower latency for chatbot serving and 6.5-fold higher throughput for synthetic-data generation. These are results for the evaluated applications. The central lesson is that a prediction tailored to the scheduling decision can deliver substantial value without solving the harder problem of exact generation-length prediction.
neurips-2024-efficient-llm-scheduling-by.tldr: Ranking likely response lengths enables more efficient LLM scheduling, with reported gains in chatbot latency and synthetic-data throughput.

paragraphs: Rigid-body motion combines continuous evolution with abrupt changes during collisions. The paper argues that existing graph neural network simulators struggle to capture this combination and often overlook the relationship between individual mesh nodes and whole objects. EGODE is designed to represent both the timing of motion and this hierarchy of physical structure.

The system maintains representations at two levels: mesh nodes and objects. A coupled graph ordinary differential equation evolves both representations over time, connecting their continuous dynamics. An additional event module estimates when collisions occur and updates the states at both levels to account for the resulting instantaneous changes.

This division gives the model explicit mechanisms for smooth motion and collision events while keeping local and object-level descriptions connected. Experiments across multiple benchmark datasets report better performance than several leading comparison methods. The findings support the proposed combination of hierarchical representations, continuous-time evolution, and event handling for the rigid-dynamics problems evaluated in the paper.
neurips-2024-egode-an-event-attended-gra.tldr: EGODE combines continuous graph dynamics with collision events at mesh-node and object levels to improve rigid-body simulation.

paragraphs: HippoRAG addresses the difficulty of integrating substantial new information into an LLM system after pre-training. Its design draws inspiration from hippocampal indexing theory, which describes roles for different brain structures in long-term memory. The aim is to make retrieval support deeper connections across new experiences.

The framework combines language models, knowledge graphs, and Personalized PageRank. Together, these components organize information and retrieve through its relationships, reflecting the complementary memory roles that motivate the design. The authors evaluate this approach on multi-hop question answering, where answering a question requires connecting multiple pieces of information.

HippoRAG improves over leading retrieval-augmented methods by up to 20% in the reported comparisons. Its single-step retrieval matches or exceeds iterative retrieval such as IRCoT while being 10–20 times cheaper and 6–13 times faster. Adding HippoRAG to IRCoT produces further gains. These findings suggest that stronger connections within retrieval can reduce repeated retrieval work while also complementing an iterative approach.
neurips-2024-hipporag-neurobiologically-.tldr: HippoRAG connects language models, knowledge graphs, and graph-based retrieval to improve multi-hop question answering efficiently.

paragraphs: Before drawing causal conclusions from a dynamical system, researchers need to establish whether its underlying structure can be identified from observations. This paper studies that question for linear ordinary differential equations when hidden variables also influence the system. Such variables complicate the connection between what is observed and the causal system producing it.

The analysis begins with hidden confounders that have no causal relationships with one another and evolve according to specified functional forms, such as polynomials in time. It then considers a more involved setting in which hidden variables have causal dependencies represented by a directed acyclic graph.

For the second setting, the authors examine different observation conditions: continuous or discrete measurements, and data from one or multiple trajectories. Simulations support the theoretical findings. The contribution is an identifiability analysis tied to explicit assumptions about hidden dynamics and available observations, helping establish when causal reasoning about these linear systems has an adequate foundation.
neurips-2024-identifiability-analysis-of.tldr: The paper analyzes identifiability in linear dynamical systems under structured hidden confounders and several observation conditions.

paragraphs: The paper examines jailbreak evaluation when an LLM is surrounded by moderation filters. Some harmful questions trigger those filters or processing errors, yet existing red-teaming benchmarks often leave such questions out. This omission makes it difficult to assess attacks against the complete guarded system.

The authors introduce JAMBench, containing 160 manually written instructions across four major risk categories and several severity levels. They also propose JAM, an attack that targets input and output moderation separately. At a high level, it combines input prefixes with cipher-character outputs produced using a fine-tuned shadow model intended to function like the guardrail model.

Experiments on four LLMs report approximately 19.88 times the jailbreak success of baselines and filtered-out rates about one-sixth as large. These findings concern the tested systems and comparisons. The research contribution combines a benchmark that explicitly exercises moderation guardrails with evidence that guardrail behavior needs direct evaluation alongside the underlying model's responses.
neurips-2024-jailbreaking-large-language.tldr: JAMBench and JAM evaluate weaknesses in LLM moderation guardrails, reporting substantially higher attack success across four tested models.

paragraphs: World models help reinforcement-learning agents plan and explore by predicting how an environment changes. Their usefulness depends on the experiences stored in the replay buffer. This paper focuses on a gap in generalization: a model may struggle with transitions backward along a recorded trajectory or between states drawn from different trajectories.

MUN is a goal-directed exploration algorithm designed to model transitions between arbitrary subgoal states within that buffer. It supports learning policies that navigate between key states, extending the connections an agent can make among its recorded experiences. This is particularly relevant when rewards are sparse and effective exploration is difficult.

The experiments report more reliable world models and substantially better policy generalization to new goal settings. The result supports learning useful connections across stored experiences, including connections that are difficult for existing world models. The scope of the stated capability is navigation among subgoal states in the replay buffer; the method's name does not imply unrestricted knowledge of every possible environment state.
neurips-2024-learning-world-models-for-u.tldr: MUN improves goal navigation by learning transitions among subgoal states across an agent's stored trajectories.

paragraphs: MeshFormer reconstructs textured 3D meshes from a small number of views. The paper argues that reconstruction models benefit from stronger built-in structure reflecting the three-dimensional nature of their task. Its design incorporates that structure through the feature representation, input guidance, and training supervision.

Features are stored in sparse 3D voxels, and the network combines Transformers with 3D convolutions. Alongside RGB images, it takes normal maps as input and predicts corresponding normal maps. These maps describe surface orientation and can be supplied by a 2D diffusion model, helping guide and refine the learned geometry.

Training combines signed-distance-function supervision with surface rendering, enabling direct mesh learning without a complicated sequence of training stages. The authors report efficient training and high-quality textured meshes with fine geometric detail. MeshFormer can also be combined with 2D diffusion models for fast single-image-to-3D and text-to-3D generation. The contribution links explicit spatial structure and geometric guidance to both reconstruction quality and training efficiency.
neurips-2024-meshformer-high-quality-mes.tldr: MeshFormer uses explicit 3D features, surface-normal guidance, and geometric supervision to efficiently reconstruct detailed textured meshes.

paragraphs: MmCows provides synchronized measurements for studying dairy-cattle monitoring with multiple sensing methods. The motivation is that relatively few datasets combine the available technologies, limiting research on how they can complement one another. The dataset brings together information about animal behavior, physiology, and the surrounding environment.

It includes two weeks of wearable and implantable sensor data from ten milking Holstein cows, using ultra-wideband, inertial, and body-temperature sensors. Four cameras contribute 4.8 million high-resolution image frames. Additional measurements cover environmental temperature and humidity, milk yield, and outdoor weather conditions.

One full day of imagery has ground-truth annotations: 20,000 frames containing 213,000 bounding boxes for 16 cows, together with 3D positions and behavior labels. The paper analyzes the sensing modalities individually and examines their complementary benefits. Its main contribution is a dataset and benchmark foundation for testing multimodal monitoring methods, supporting research relevant to animal welfare, farm productivity, and sustainable dairy farming.
neurips-2024-mmcows-a-multimodal-dataset.tldr: MmCows combines synchronized animal sensors, cameras, and environmental measurements to support multimodal dairy-cattle monitoring research.

paragraphs: A navigable graph lets a search reach any target node from any starting node by repeatedly choosing the neighbor closest to the destination. Connecting every pair of points makes this easy, but creates many edges. This paper studies how sparse such graphs can be for high-dimensional point sets.

The authors give an efficient construction whose average degree is O(sqrt(n log n)) for n points. It applies in any dimension and with any distance function. The guarantee therefore provides a broadly applicable way to construct a graph that supports this greedy routing rule while using fewer connections than a complete graph.

A nearly matching lower bound shows that some high-dimensional point sets require many edges. Even for Euclidean distance in O(log n) dimensions, a random point set admits no navigable graph with average degree O(n^alpha) for alpha below one-half. The proof shows that nearby regions around random points overlap too little to share enough routing connections, establishing a structural limit on sparsity.
neurips-2024-navigable-graphs-for-high-d.tldr: The paper constructs sparse navigable graphs for arbitrary point sets and proves a nearly matching high-dimensional sparsity limit.

paragraphs: Temporal action segmentation divides a sequence into action segments. Context across time helps distinguish those actions, and offline systems can gather that context after viewing the entire sequence. OnlineTAS tackles the harder setting in which the sequence is processed as it unfolds and the full temporal context is unavailable.

The framework uses an adaptive memory to retain useful context while accommodating changes over time. A feature-augmentation module then combines that memory with frame features, allowing segmentation decisions to use the evolving context. The authors additionally introduce post-processing to reduce the severe over-segmentation that occurs in the online setting.

These components address related problems: maintaining relevant history and avoiding excessive fragmentation into action segments. The authors present the framework as the first online approach to temporal action segmentation and report state-of-the-art performance on three common benchmarks. The findings support adaptive context handling as a practical basis for segmentation when decisions must be made during the sequence.
neurips-2024-onlinetas-an-online-baselin.tldr: OnlineTAS uses adaptive memory and post-processing to improve action segmentation while a sequence unfolds.

paragraphs: OpenSatMap is a satellite-image dataset intended to support large-scale map construction. Extracting road structures from satellite imagery offers an efficient route to building maps for transportation applications. The paper identifies a data bottleneck: existing datasets have relatively low-resolution images and coarse labels that limit the detail researchers can learn to recover.

The dataset supplies instance-level annotations and level-20 imagery, compared with the level-19 maximum described for existing datasets. Instance annotations distinguish individual instances rather than providing only broad semantic categories. The authors also emphasize data diversity and describe OpenSatMap as the largest dataset of its kind at the time of the work.

OpenSatMap geographically covers and aligns with nuScenes and Argoverse 2, creating a potential connection to autonomous-driving research. Its contribution is a benchmark resource for learning and evaluating detailed satellite-based mapping. The alignment may support downstream driving applications, while the abstract presents that benefit as a possibility rather than a demonstrated improvement in autonomous-driving performance.
neurips-2024-opensatmap-a-fine-grained-h.tldr: OpenSatMap supplies high-resolution satellite imagery and instance-level annotations for detailed mapping, with alignment to autonomous-driving datasets.

paragraphs: Diffusion image generation repeatedly estimates and removes noise from an initially random input. Running a neural network many times makes this process costly in latency and energy on digital hardware. This paper explores implementing the denoising computation through the propagation of light in a transparent medium.

The framework sends noisy image patterns through passive diffractive optical layers. Together, the layers transmit the predicted noise component needed for denoising. Their properties are trained through an online procedure that backpropagates error through an analytical model of the optical system, connecting the desired computation to the behavior of the light.

Once trained, the same passive layers are reused across denoising steps. The authors demonstrate this optical formulation and describe it as enabling fast image generation with minimal power consumption through the bandwidth and efficiency of optical processing. The contribution is a physical implementation of a repeated diffusion computation, with the learned optical structure remaining fixed as the denoising process proceeds.
neurips-2024-optical-diffusion-models-fo.tldr: Trained passive optical layers predict diffusion noise terms, enabling high-speed image generation with minimal power consumption.

paragraphs: This paper studies stochastic convex optimization under differential privacy when gradients can have heavy tails. Instead of requiring every sample function to have a uniformly bounded Lipschitz constant, it assumes a bounded kth moment of those constants. This permits occasional large values while retaining statistical control over their distribution.

A new reduction-based approach achieves rates that are optimal up to logarithmic factors under approximate differential privacy. The error combines a statistical term, G2 divided by sqrt(n), with a privacy-related term, Gk times (sqrt(d)/(n epsilon)) raised to 1 minus 1/k. Here the moment bounds, sample count, dimension, and privacy parameter determine the trade-off.

The bound nearly matches an existing lower bound, with an additional mild polylogarithmic dependence on the approximate-privacy parameter delta. The authors also give stronger algorithmic results under additional assumptions: optimality with a known Lipschitz constant, near-linear runtime for smooth functions, and optimal linear-time performance for smooth generalized linear models. These refinements depend on their respective assumptions.
neurips-2024-private-stochastic-convex-o.tldr: A reduction-based approach achieves nearly optimal private convex-optimization error under moment bounds that allow heavy-tailed gradients.

paragraphs: Post-training quantization stores LLM weights with fewer bits, reducing memory requirements and potentially increasing inference throughput when memory movement is the bottleneck. Recent approaches quantize several weights together to use the available representation more effectively. However, their vector-quantization codebooks grow exponentially with the number of jointly encoded weights.

QTIP uses trellis-coded quantization to overcome this obstacle to high-dimensional quantization. Its stateful decoder separates codebook size from bitrate and effective dimension. This allows the representation to account for much larger groups of weights without requiring the exponentially growing codebook that limits existing vector-based approaches to dimensions of eight or less.

The method includes several trellis-code designs, ranging from lookup-only implementations to computed versions that require no lookup table. These designs fit a hardware-efficient bitshift trellis structure. The authors report state-of-the-art quantization quality and inference speed, supporting a design that treats compression quality and efficient decoding as connected requirements for practical LLM inference.
neurips-2024-qtip-quantization-with-trel.tldr: QTIP uses trellis-coded quantization to compress LLM weights in high dimensions while maintaining efficient decoding and strong inference performance.

paragraphs: Self-interested reinforcement-learning agents can settle into social outcomes that leave everyone worse off than cooperation would. Existing opponent-shaping methods try to influence how other agents learn, but may require privileged knowledge of their learning algorithms or expensive exploration of higher-level learning dynamics. This paper proposes an alternative based on reciprocity.

The proposed agents, called Reciprocators, are intrinsically motivated to respond to how opponents' actions affect their returns. They seek to increase an opponent's return after behavior beneficial to the Reciprocator and decrease it after detrimental behavior. This is intended to shift opponents' learned action values toward mutually beneficial choices.

The approach avoids directly differentiating through a model of the opponent's policy and is presented as learning-rule agnostic and sample efficient. The authors show that Reciprocators can encourage cooperation in social dilemmas extending over time while agents learn simultaneously. The result establishes a demonstrated route to cooperation in those settings, without claiming that reciprocity guarantees cooperation in every interaction.
neurips-2024-reciprocal-reward-influence.tldr: Reciprocator agents encourage cooperation by responding to opponents' beneficial and harmful actions through reciprocal effects on returns.

paragraphs: When labeling nodes in a network is expensive, active learning aims to choose a useful subset to query. This paper proposes an offline selection method that uses both network connections and node covariates. Its central concern is choosing nodes that reveal useful structure while also supporting reliable predictions when the available information is noisy.

The method uses two-stage biased sampling, drawing on graph signal recovery and random spectral sparsification. It balances informativeness, meaning the complexity of graph signals learnable from queried responses, with representativeness, meaning the selected nodes' ability to control generalization error under noisy node-level information. These objectives need to be considered together.

The authors establish a theoretical relationship between generalization error and the number of selected nodes, revealing a trade-off between the two objectives. Numerical experiments show competitive performance against existing graph active-learning methods, especially when covariates and responses contain noise. The method applies to both regression and classification, making the selection strategy relevant to different types of node prediction.
neurips-2024-robust-offline-active-learn.tldr: A two-stage graph sampling method balances informativeness and representativeness to select useful labels, particularly under noisy node information.

paragraphs: An answer can be factually correct while still being unclear, irrelevant, or difficult to interpret. SubjECTive-QA studies these qualities in earnings-call question-and-answer sessions, where company representatives' responses invite subjective judgments. The dataset provides 49,446 human annotations covering assertiveness, caution, optimism, specificity, clarity, and relevance.

The authors evaluate language models on these six dimensions. RoBERTa-base, the strongest pretrained language model in their comparison, has weighted F1 scores similar to Llama-3-70b-Chat on lower-subjectivity features such as relevance and clarity, with a mean difference of 2.17%. For higher-subjectivity features such as specificity and assertiveness, the abstract reports a larger mean difference of 10.01%.

To examine transfer beyond finance, the researchers test on questions and answers from White House press briefings and gaggles. Using their best model for each feature yields an average weighted F1 of 65.97%. This supports broader applicability while grounding the claim in a specific additional setting. The dataset makes several dimensions of answer quality available for systematic study beyond factual correctness.
neurips-2024-subjective-qa-measuring-sub.tldr: SubjECTive-QA provides human annotations for six subjective answer qualities and evaluates their prediction within and beyond earnings calls.

paragraphs: Training-data sampling determines how likely each example is to be used during learning. A useful sampler can help a neural network converge to a strong solution, but searching for one can involve many expensive trials. Swift Sampler aims to make that search efficient enough for large datasets.

The method represents a sampler through a small set of hyperparameters, with the title emphasizing ten parameters. It also evaluates candidate samplers using an approximation to a local minimum. Together, these choices reduce the size of the search problem and the computational effort needed to estimate whether a candidate sampling strategy is promising.

Experiments across several tasks report performance improvements, including a 1.5% improvement on ImageNet, and show that learned sampling strategies can transfer between different neural networks. The stated benefit is therefore broader than finding one useful sampler for one model. The results support a compact, inexpensive search procedure as a practical way to learn training-data sampling probabilities automatically.
neurips-2024-swift-sampler-efficient-lea.tldr: Swift Sampler makes automatic data-sampling search inexpensive through compact parameterization and approximate candidate evaluation.

paragraphs: Validating a global climate model requires comparing its outputs with observational and reanalysis data. This paper introduces spherical convolutional Wasserstein distance as a way to make that comparison more spatially informative. The measure is designed to account for geographic variability while quantifying differences in the local distributions of climate variables.

The method uses convolutional projections to incorporate spatial information into the comparison. Its focus on local distributions makes the assessment sensitive to how climate variables differ across locations. This provides a framework for examining discrepancies between model output and reference data while retaining information about their spatial structure.

The authors apply the measure to historical outputs from members of the Coupled Model Intercomparison Project and compare phase 5 with phase 6. They find modest improvements in phase 6 models' ability to reproduce realistic climatologies. The result provides evidence of incremental progress under this evaluation, alongside a new distribution-based tool for assessing global climate-model output.
neurips-2024-validating-climate-models-w.tldr: A spatially informed distributional distance evaluates climate models and finds modest climatology improvements from CMIP5 to CMIP6.
